To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fatigue life of solder interconnect in BGA packages can be accurately predicted using the fracture mechanics approach.

(1) BGA interconnects fail by crack initiation and propagation at the nickel/solder interfaces; (2) the crack initiation and propagation phases are stable and the acceleration phase is unstable; (3) the crack initiation, propagation and acceleration percentages are on the order of, respectively, 15%, 50%, and 35%; (4) the number of cycles required for failure is frequency-independent in the range of 50–100 Hz; (5) damage mechanics fatigue life

the failure of BGA solder interconnects under vibration fatigue is the result of crack propagation along the nickel/gold/solder interface, that the failure is frequency-independent for frequencies ranging from 25 to 100 kHz, and that a fracture mechanics model can predict the failure life of BGA solder joints with a factor of two accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fatigue life prediction of BGA packages subjected to high cycle vibration loading.
the development and application of experimental and numerical techniques to the study of fatigue in BGA interconnects.
the development of a new experimental technique for high cycle fatigue testing of BGA packages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a fracture mechanics model can be used to accurately predict the fatigue life of BGA solder joints subjected to high-cycle vibration.
a nonlinear fracture mechanics model is a good candidate for the life prediction of BGA packages under high cycle fatigue loading.
the fracture mechanics approach is more appropriate than the damage mechanics approach for predicting the high-cycle fatigue life of BGA interconnects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatigue life of BGA interconnects under vibration loading is governed by crack initiation, stable crack propagation and accelerated crack propagation.
the fracture mechanics approach is a viable and promising technique for the prediction of solder interconnect fatigue life.
the fracture model is the best choice for predicting fatigue life of BGA packages.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a nonlinear finite element model, which includes the effects of solder plasticity and the nonlinear elastic behavior of the nickel underlayer, provides a good prediction of crack propagation and the number of vibration cycles required to failure.

the fatigue failure of solder interconnect in BGA packages is a complex process involving the initiation, stable propagation, and accelerated propagation of cracks at the interface between the solder joint and the copper pad.
the failure of the solder interconnects is a fracture mechanics phenomenon, and the fracture mechanics approach provides the best correlation with test data.
